package_info.why_malicious: NextCry is a ransomware strain that targets Linux servers running NextCloud by exploiting a vulnerability in the NGINX configuration, encrypting user files and demanding ransom for decryption. Its behavior is overtly malicious, as it is designed to extort victims by denying access to their own data.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (post-exploitation after remote code execution via NGINX vulnerability)
execution_context.file_location: Deployed on compromised NextCloud server (location varies, often /tmp or user-writable directory)
required_permissions: network (optional, for ransom note delivery or C2)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: for file in $(find /home/nextcloud/data -type f); do openssl enc -aes-256-ctr -salt -in "$file" -out "$file.nextcry" -k <random_key>; rm "$file"; done
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code iterates over user files in the NextCloud data directory, encrypts each file using AES-256-CTR via OpenSSL, appends a .nextcry extension, and deletes the original file, resulting in user data being rendered inaccessible.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code performs mass encryption of user files and deletes the originals, a hallmark of ransomware activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal server-side scripts should not encrypt user data en masse or delete original files without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or archival scripts may encrypt files, but would not delete originals without explicit backup/restore logic and user approval.
key_indicators: Bulk file encryption in user data directories
Deletion of original files after encryption
Use of strong symmetric encryption with random keys

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits a vulnerability in the NextCloud NGINX configuration to gain remote code execution on the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment and execution of ransomware payload

attack_chain.action: Ransomware payload is executed, scanning for user files in the NextCloud data directory.
Files are encrypted and originals deleted, with ransom note left for the victim.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim is extorted for decryption key

behavioral_signatures: Bulk encryption of files in NextCloud data directories
Mass deletion of original files after encryption
file_indicators: Sudden disappearance of large numbers of user files
Presence of ransom note files (e.g., README or INSTRUCTION files)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known ransomware C2 infrastructure (if present)
Unusual traffic following exploitation of NGINX/NextCloud
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for mass file modifications and deletions in NextCloud data directories, especially the creation of files with the .nextcry extension. Alert on execution of OpenSSL or similar encryption tools by the web server user. Look for signs of exploitation of the NGINX FastCGI vulnerability (CVE-2019-11043) and subsequent suspicious process launches. File integrity monitoring and behavioral analytics can help detect rapid, automated file encryption and deletion.
